description.narrative: RWIs arbete går ut på att stödja Kenya Prison Service att integrera mänskliga rättigheter i arbetet på ett antal pilotfängelser.

Raoul Wallenberg Institute Kenya programme is focussing on supporting Kenya Prison Service to integrate a human rights perspective at a number of pilot prisons. Human rights Audits are being carried out and thereafter implemented.

General question: Results related to the intended outcome 2015Question: Summarise results related to the intended outcome (this information will be sent to Open Aid)Answer: The activity period of this programme stretched from January 2012 - March 2015. The overall objective was to support human rights reforms in implementing the new Constitution of Kenya and operationalizing key policy priorities and strategies, in line with international standards, in particular regarding impartial and efficient administration of justice. The programme had two components with the following objectives:
Component 1: Strengthening Human Rights Capacity in the Kenya Prison Service (KPS) with the objective to create sustainable capacity within KPS to meet relevant international human rights standards in particular the UN Standard MInimum Rules for the Treatment of Prisoners (UN SMRs), through targeted interventions with the KPS Human Rights Office and Prison Staff Training College. Component 2: Strengtening Human Rights Perspectives in the Coordination between Administration of Justice Actors, with the objective to contribute to enhanced human rights perspectives in efforts for a coordinated, effective and consultative approach in the administration of justice and reform of the justice system in Kenya.
In line with the original plans, the bulk of the programme concerned Component 1 and the human rights development work with the KPS, while Component 2 only included a few, more limited interventions in the area of justice coordination and administration. Overall, the programme has achieved the intended results.
The programme has had a high results achievement both at outcome- and output level. The main results of the programme was verified by an independent evaluation that was carried out in 2014 and can be summarized as follows:: - Development of a core body of KPS Human Rights Officers, at national, regional and institutional levels, with the ability to independently conduct human rights assessments, deliver human rights trainings, and facilitate the development of human rights action plans. - A demonstrated increase in compliance with relevant international human rights standards, in particular the UN SMRs, in KPS as a whole, and a selection of pilot institutions in particular. - More informed reform initiatives, policies and programmes in terms of responsiveness to human rights, stakeholder needs and context within and between justice sector institutions.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
